method: After freezing the pair, reopened Articles 3.8–3.9 and Appendix I and the UCM catalogue core and research-methods entries. findings: The single-domain example is 180 EC. Appendix I controls the four named 5 EC courses and the 7.5 and 5 EC core projects. Three 2.5 EC core skills trainings complete the 20 EC skills-and-project allocation. The remaining components are 15 general education, 75 concentration courses, 15 concentration skills, 15 concentration projects and 20 Capstone. General education spans both outside domains in this example. An approved interdisciplinary concentration instead has 5–10 EC in the third domain. Article 3.9 limits introductory concentration courses to 20 EC and requires at least 20 advanced EC across at least three courses, and one advanced concentration project.

Catalogue SKI1004 and SKI1005 develop research questions and then a feasible proposal and qualitative techniques for PRO1012. Academic Skills I and II train academic writing and argument in the first year. The 20 EC Capstone begins only after at least 140 EC. The catalogue also lists COR1006 as core and retains some references to it, but Appendix I specifically enumerates the four mandatory courses and names COR1007, also present in the 2026–27 catalogue.

Both the external credit illustration and each scheduled UCR composition total 180 EC. Maastricht’s sample allocation is for one domain. The research proposal and qualitative methods substantiate the partial Methods II alignment, while the required project stays separate. The UCR lab builds practical skills after the gateway and the health option supplies science research depth. The politics option retains its cross-domain focus and closest common-core overlap. The humanities option retains its distinct interpretive and media focus.
